candidates.change_summary: Remove the overflow check require statement so balances can overflow and wrap around, altering the final balance.
Delete the balance increment so the deposit has no effect on the caller's balance.
Change the assignment to always set the balance to msg.value instead of adding it, overwriting any previous balance.
Change the balance update to subtract msg.value instead of adding it.
Insert a line before the balance update that resets the caller's balance to zero, so the final balance is only msg.value instead of the sum.

Replace the balance precondition `balances[msg.sender]>=_am` with `balances[msg.sender]<=_am`, weakening the guard so a Collect calls the external call and writes balance only when the requested amount is at least the caller's balance.
Move the balance subtraction state update from before the external call to after the external call succeeds, leaving the observable balance change inside the call window differing from the original.

Replace the balance subtraction `balances[msg.sender] - _am` with `balances[msg.sender] + _am`, causing the caller's balance to increase after a successful Collect when the original guard is satisfied.
Delete the revert in the failed external call branch, so a failed call no longer reverts the transaction and the earlier balance subtraction persists.

Changed the guard from `balances[msg.sender]>=MinSum && balances[msg.sender]>=_am` to `balances[msg.sender]>=MinSum || balances[msg.sender]>=_am`, weakening it so Collect can proceed for large requested amounts when the balance only satisfies MinSum.
Deleted the balance subtraction before the external call, so the caller's balance is not reduced and the observable balance/call outcome can differ after reentrancy or successful collection.

Moved the state update `balances[msg.sender] = balances[msg.sender] - _am;` from before the external call to after it, exposing the old balance to the callee during the call and allowing reentrancy-based double collection.
